q: The prefix-free (Shannon) code length for a symbol x with probability p(x) is optimally −log₂ p(x) bits. The Kraft inequality states that a prefix-free code with lengths {lᵢ} exists if and only if:
exp: Kraft inequality: Σ 2^{-lᵢ} ≤ 1 is necessary and sufficient for prefix-free codes. Conversely, for any lengths satisfying Kraft's inequality, a prefix-free code exists. Combined with H(X) ≤ ∑ pᵢlᵢ < H(X)+1, this bounds the overhead of Huffman coding.
